sticky.scrollLinked.reducedMotionCaveat: VERIFIED INACCURATE CLAIM CORRECTED (Round 3): this role's `position: sticky` behavior is NOT disabled under prefers-reduced-motion in the live build. Checked directly against the served bundle (component---src-pages-property-management-tsx-*.js): there is no `matchMedia`/JS-level reduced-motion check anywhere in it, and none of its several `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS blocks touch the `position:sticky` declaration -- they only reset transform/opacity/transition on unrelated decorative layers. The global tokens.css 0.01ms animation/transition-duration collapse (see reducedMotionFallback below) cannot affect `position` either, since position is not an animatable duration/transition property. The only thing that actually disables the sticky pin is a viewport-width breakpoint on mobile (an unrelated responsive fallback, not a motion-preference one). sections/sticky-feature-showcase.json previously claimed this was 'REQUIRED — static stacked layout (position:sticky removed)' under reduced motion; that description was not measured against real behavior and has been corrected to flag this as an open accessibility gap rather than a shipped fallback.

reducedMotionFallback: Every role above must resolve to the global tokens.css @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block: animation-duration/transition-duration forced to 0.01ms, scroll-behavior:auto. Any generated section using a motion role must set reducedMotionFallback per schema/pagespec.schema.json. VERIFIED against the served build's assets/tokens/tokens.css (Round 3) -- the block's four declarations match exactly. Note this mechanism can only ever affect animation/transition timing; it cannot alter a persistent layout property like `position: sticky` (see sticky.scrollLinked's reducedMotionCaveat above) -- any role relying on a non-animation CSS property needs its own explicit override to have a real reduced-motion fallback.
